### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **13** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-memory`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/knowledge-memory`, `@objectstack/knowledge-ragflow`, `@objectstack/plugin-dev`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **114** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **13** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/package.json`, `packages/core/src/egress.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/vitest.config.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d01f399e3b741c8e0d54b811b5d6e29551151509`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **13** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/package.json`, `packages/core/src/egress.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/vitest.config.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- **42** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **189** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d01f399e3b741c8e0d54b811b5d6e29551151509` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c13c83793faf5d2c5ae2828423da17800b06a797` — the merge of head `dfef79b5ced76e092098e3fca5d20e1f48665503` into base `d01f399e3b741c8e0d54b811b5d6e29551151509`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c13c83793faf5d2c5ae2828423da17800b06a797 && git checkout c13c83793faf5d2c5ae2828423da17800b06a797
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d01f399e3b741c8e0d54b811b5d6e29551151509 dfef79b5ced76e092098e3fca5d20e1f48665503 && git checkout -B drift-repro d01f399e3b741c8e0d54b811b5d6e29551151509 && git merge --no-ff dfef79b5ced76e092098e3fca5d20e1f48665503

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d01f399e3b741c8e0d54b811b5d6e29551151509
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d01f399e3b741c8e0d54b811b5d6e29551151509` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

No prior contract-review record exists for this PR, so no earlier finding id is continued; M1, S1 to S3 and N1 to N3 are all new on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Declaration.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial on both the PR body and the changeset and agree with the diff: nothing an author can write is added, removed or re-valued; what moves is which destinations two outbound doors may reach, decided by operator environment at boot. The ADR-0087 `not-required` disposition holds for the same reason.
- **Doors named in the declaration.** Webhook deliveries and durable flow callouts have one send site in `service-messaging` and its default is the guard; the flow `http` node's inline arm, which is also the durable arm's no-outbox fallback, has one send site in `service-automation` and it is the guard. No second send site exists in either package or in `plugin-webhooks` on this head. No shipped plugin reaches either send site without the guard. Held.
- **Decision at the moment of connection.** The verdict is taken on the addresses the connection is made to, the connection goes to a judged address without a second resolution, each redirect hop is judged, a policy that throws refuses, and no caller can substitute its own transport. Held.
- **Boot.** A malformed or over-broad allowlist fails init in all three plugins; there is no unguarded fallback and no `NODE_ENV` branch. Held.
- **Controls.** Each refusal family has a paired control that delivers (allowlisted address, allowlisted host, allowed redirect, non-refusal transport failure still retried), the implementer's ablation of the refusal turned the three sending suites red, and the fixtures open loopback through the environment only. The readings in the PR body were taken at `28edf362a`; the two later commits and the merge are covered by this head's CI, not by those readings.
- **The rule's never tier and its "public" word.** Not held as declared: M1 and S1 below.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on all five packages with the BREAKING banner, the Who-moves paragraph and the one-line fix: correct for a non-protocol narrowing under AGENTS.md (the level follows the metadata kind, which is `none`). The new `@objectstack/core/egress` subpath, the three `egressPolicy` options and the two ledger codes are additive and ride the same level; `undici` is a runtime dependency of `@objectstack/core` and the lockfile agrees.

CI on this head: 69 check-runs, all completed, 60 success, 9 skipped, none failing or pending. The PR is open and mergeable-clean against `main`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **First-wave scope (dev flag).** Accepted as ruled for the two named doors. Escalated to the seat: the review inputs carry no tracking reference for the follow-up wave, so the seat confirms it is tracked in the private lane before landing; see S3 for the wording that must not outrun the scope meanwhile.
- **Proxy (dev flag).** These requests no longer use an environment-configured HTTP proxy. It is stated in the changeset's For-hosts paragraph; answered, with the note that it is an operator-facing change sitting under a hosts heading.
- **Not measured: a real public target (dev flag).** Not accepted as closed: see S2, which is exactly the part a stand-in on one loopback address cannot show.
- **Dogfood battery (dev flag).** Owed on the final head; the seat carries the reading before landing.
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- **SQL push-down.** No new id materialisation and no in-app join. The boot census reads `sys_webhook` once and judges each row in the application because the judgement needs name resolution, which no query can push down; see N3 for its unbounded read.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes real a refusal the platform owed and takes away, at the consumer, only what the declaration names: internal targets need an operator allowlist entry. The seam (one decision per connected address, with host, organization and source, fail-closed) is the right shape and mirrors the datasource connect policy. Against the rule as written, the head does not yet hold in four places. Mechanism-level detail for M1 and S1 is in the sealed notes only.

- M1 (must-fix) — The rule says cloud metadata addresses are never reachable and can never be allowlisted. The default policy's never tier does not hold that for the whole class the rule names. Complete the tier and pin each added member both ways (refused by default, refused under a covering allowlist entry) with a neighbouring control. Specifics: sealed notes, M1.
- S1 (should-fix) — The rule's sentence is "only public addresses"; the default policy decides by an enumerated set of classes, and the two do not coincide. Either make the classification answer the sentence, or restate the sentence everywhere as the enumerated classes the Clause-② line already lists. Specifics: sealed notes, S1.
- S2 (should-fix) — The changeset promises that requests to public targets are unaffected, and the PR body records that delivery to a real public target was not measured. The guard dials one of the addresses it judged and does not fall back to the others, which the bare fetch it replaces did. A public target that answers on more than one address or family can therefore fail where it delivered before. Dial the judged addresses in turn, or state the changed behaviour in Who-moves; add a control with a first address that does not accept and a second that does.
- S3 (should-fix) — The changeset body and the policy's own header state the rule for every outbound request a tenant can aim, while the scope ruled for this PR is two doors. The release note must claim what ships: scope those sentences to webhook deliveries and the flow `http` node, as the title, the Clause-② line and the boot line already do. Prose-face and jsdoc only.
- N1 (nit) — The connect-time re-judgement of the socket's own remote address has no pin; the dial-the-judged-address property is pinned only indirectly, through the controls.
- N2 (nit) — In `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts` the new `bootEgressCensus` sits between `bootWebhookTable` and its jsdoc, so that comment now documents the wrong method.
- N3 (nit) — The census reads every `sys_webhook` row, whole, with no projection or bound; and the default guard keeps the logger of whichever plugin installed it first.

M1 and S1 to S3 are open. A delta read by this reviewer is owed on the next head.

Second record on this PR; the first (comment 6908879722) was a FAIL on an earlier head. This head is judged in full. Independence: this session neither dispatched nor implemented the diff. Findings are stated at rule level; specifics are in the sealed notes only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What moves from sent to refused.** A webhook delivery, a durable flow callout and a flow `http` node request (inline arm, and the durable arm's no-outbox fallback) whose connected address is not public are refused unless the operator's allowlist names the target; the never tier is refused whatever the allowlist says. - **What the ledger gains.** `EGRESS_REFUSED` and `EGRESS_ALLOWLIST_INVALID`, both under `@objectstack/core`, both additive; the derived `ErrorCode` enum widens by exactly these two and the generated reference pages agree. Named right.

- **Not held as declared.** The changeset and the boot line state the rule without a runtime condition, and the tree does not make the rule hold unconditionally: M2 below.
- **Decision on what is connected to.** Every resolved address is judged before any dial, the dial goes to a judged address with no second resolution, the connected socket's own remote address is judged again, every redirect hop is judged, and forms that carry another address are judged as what they carry. Held where the guard is in the path.
- **Controls.** Each refusal family has a paired control that delivers; the never tier is pinned both ways with neighbours; the fixtures open loopback through the environment only, and no production branch reads the test environment. The vitest edits add a source alias and weaken no isolation; the lockfile adds one dependency under core.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on all five packages with `!`, the BREAKING banner, the Who-moves paragraph and its one-line fix, and one ADR-0087 `not-required` marker: correct under AGENTS.md on main for a non-protocol narrowing (`Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` and keeps the banner and the disposition). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial on the PR body and the changeset and agree with the diff: nothing an author can write is added, removed or re-valued. The new `@objectstack/core/egress` subpath, the three `egressPolicy` options and the two ledger codes are additive and ride the same level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **First-wave scope (dev flag).** The diff guards two doors and the PR body names the outbound doors that stay unjudged. The ruling behind "as ruled" is not among this review's inputs, so it is escalated: the seat confirms the ruling and that the follow-up wave is tracked in the private lane before landing. Until that wave lands, sibling doors in the same authoring surface remain outside the rule, exactly as the PR body already states.
- **Proxy (dev flag).** Answered: now stated under Who moves.
- **Not measured: a real public target (dev flag).** The multi-address half is answered by the dial-in-turn pins. The runtime half is not: see M2.
- **Dogfood battery (dev flag).** `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on this head.
- **Author.** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- **SQL push-down.** No new id materialisation and no in-app join. The boot census reads three projected columns in capped, ordered pages and judges in the application because the judgement needs name resolution, which no query can push down.

### ④ Design judgment

The ledger change holds against its consumers: two additive codes under the owning package, carried by the two error classes the comment cites, neither on a wire envelope. The seam (one decision per connected address with host, organization and source; a throw is a refusal; a malformed or over-broad allowlist fails the boot in all three plugins; no unguarded fallback in the plugin wiring) is the right shape, and the narrowing takes away only what it declares, behind a followable operator opt-in. One part of the contract does not hold.

S1: closed.
S2: closed.
S3: closed.
N1: closed.
N2: closed.

- M2 (must-fix) — The guard is not fail-closed against the process it runs in. Its enforcement depends on a property of the host runtime that install neither establishes nor verifies; where that property is absent a guarded request is sent unjudged while the boot line reports the guard active, and the repository documents deployment targets where the property is not assured. The three sending packages also gain load-time requirements on those targets that Who-moves does not state. Make enforcement independent of that property, or prove it at install and refuse the boot and every send when it cannot be proven; pin it with a case that fails if the request can leave without the policy being asked; state any runtime requirement in the changeset. Specifics: sealed notes, M2.
- N4 (nit) — The PR title states the rule for tenant-aimed outbound requests in general, while the changeset title, the Clause-② line and the boot line scope it to the two doors; the title is what a squash carries.

Third record on this PR; delta after the FAIL in comment 6912107145 on `e022b2d6`, and this head is judged in full. Independence: this session neither dispatched nor implemented the diff. Findings are stated at rule level; specifics are in the sealed notes only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What moves from sent to refused.** Unchanged from the declaration: a webhook delivery, a durable flow callout and a flow `http` node request whose connected address is not public are refused unless the operator's allowlist names the target; the never tier is refused whatever the allowlist says. Named right by the Clause-② line and the changeset.
- **Enforcement no longer rests on the host process.** The guard sends with its own transport, the same one its install-time proof exercises, and takes nothing from the process's replaceable globals. The proof passes only when a request made that way was handed to the guard's connector and failed with the connector's own answer. Where it does not pass, the install rejects, all three plugin inits await it and fail the boot, and every send is refused before a connection is attempted, including on a guard taken without the install step. Each send also refuses a response that arrived over a connection its own connector did not judge. Held.
- **Pins for it.** A runtime whose transport does not route through the connector: install refused, send refused, nothing arrives, the policy is never asked. A transport that stops routing after the proof: the response is refused. A control in the real runtime delivers and is judged before it leaves. The implementer reports each red under ablation.
- **Runtime requirement.** Stated in the changeset under its own heading, in the environment reference next to the allowlist setting, and in the guard's jsdoc and the three plugin init comments. Held.
- **What a refusal reads.** One text for every cause; a policy that answers no verdict ends as a named refusal; a host name that does not resolve reads the same text and stays retriable. The ledger's sentence for the code has not followed: S4.
- **Callers.** The install is now asynchronous; its three callers await it and no other caller exists in the tree. Suites that faked the network through the global now take a named stand-in or an allowlisted loopback receiver through the environment; no production branch reads the test environment.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on all five packages with `!`, the BREAKING banner, the Who-moves paragraph and its one-line fix, and one ADR-0087 `not-required` marker: correct under AGENTS.md on main for a non-protocol narrowing. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial on the PR body and the changeset and agree with the diff. The asynchronous install and the new readiness member on the guard are additive on a subpath that is new in this same PR. The ledger gains exactly two additive codes under `@objectstack/core`; unchanged by this round.

Check-runs on this head: all completed, each success or skipped, none failing or pending. The PR is open.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **First-wave scope (dev flag).** Still escalated: the ruling behind "as ruled" is not among this review's inputs, so the seat confirms the ruling and that the follow-up wave is tracked in the private lane before landing. The PR body names the doors that stay outside the rule.
- **Proxy (dev flag).** Answered: stated under Who moves.
- **Not measured: a real public target (dev flag).** The runtime half is now answered by the install-time proof and its pins; the multi-address half by the dial-in-turn pins. Delivery to a real public target stays unmeasured and is declared so.
- **Test-only transport option (dev flag).** Answered: marked in its jsdoc as tests only and outside the rule; no production caller passes it.
- **Dogfood battery (dev flag).** `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on this head.
- **Author.** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- **SQL push-down.** No new id materialisation and no in-app join in this round; the boot census is unchanged.
